messages.subject: GSoC-2015
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am Shubham. I would like to start contributing to rCharts and rMaps. I am interested in data science (especially data wrangling and visualization) and machine learning. I have used pure Javascript libraries like D3.js, leaflet.js etc to build visualizations. Although, I primarily use Python, I am also interested in R. As a starting point, I'm trying to resolve some issues in the libraries.
I was wondering if you would like to suggest something.

Blog: http://shubhamtomar.me/
LinkedIn: http://in.linkedin.com/in/shubhamtomar
GitHub: http://www.github.com/Autodidact24

Thanks,
Shubham Singh Tomar

> I am Shubham. I would like to start contributing to rCharts and rMaps. I

>

Shubham,

I would suggest starting by contacting the authors of rCharts and rMaps,
to see if they are interested in participating as mentors in GSoC 2015.

We won't approve projects without firm plans and qualified mentors.  We
also won't approve projects where the code written by students has no
chance of making it into a package that others can use.  So, based on
your interests, that means your next step is the authors of the packages
you're proposing to contribute to.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson

messages.subject: membership applications
messages.body_plain:
It's that time of year when random names pop up requesting membership.
If there is a comment included telling me/us who the person is and their
interest in R, I've been giving approval. I've been ignoring others.

If you are planning to mentor or advise anyone to apply, do tell them to
let us know at least some information that suggests it is worthwhile
approving them. Early on we approved everyone and got spam emails. And
there are always those who try blanket applications in the hope they'll
get lucky and get some money.

Best, JN

messages.subject: Seeking a mentor for a specific GSoC '15 project
messages.subject_clean: Seeking a mentor for a specific GSoC '15 project
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am a third-year PhD student in statistics at Missouri S&T, and my research is in the area of credit risk modeling.  I have passed the first two US actuarial exams, and currently have a research assistantship in economics for which I'm using R.

Corresponding with the authors, I have identified a likely GSoC project in the 2013 NAAJ paper (Tang and Yuan), namely about estimation of the limit measure for the tail distribution in a multivariate regular variation structure.  My generalized GSoC proposal is to write an R package to estimate such limiting measures, perhaps in a more general setting than the loss given default.

I write this email seeking a mentor for said project.  If you are interested, you may contact me at this address.

Regards,
Daniel Geiger
